thread:
maya.finance: Heads-up: CardioNova dispute inbound. They paid invoice INV-5092 but claim reserved commit didn't apply for April; they were billed full burst. They want correction and a statement for their auditors.
tom.ops: Did the capacity binding job run? We had a TZ migration on 2026-04-01 that shifted CRON windows. Could be a race where provisioning happened after the billing snapshot.
billing-bot: Invoice INV-5092 uploaded: https://invoices.redwood/INV-5092.pdf
billing-bot: Metering summary: committed_hours=0, burst_tokens=2,000,000, reserved_tag=present, tag_applied_at=2026-04-01T08:12:03Z, billing_snapshot_time=2026-04-01T07:55:00Z
elena.sales: CardioNova signed a 6 GPU-month reserved commit (contract CN-6G-2026). Sales notes provisioning scheduled for 2026-04-01 08:00 UTC. If snapshot was at 07:55 we missed the window.
maya.finance: Two options: (A) retroactively allocate reserved usage and issue a corrected invoice + ledger adjustment (requires legal sign-off), or (B) offer an SLA-style operational credit and keep invoice as-is. Need economics and approval.
zara.revenue: What's the delta if we retro-allocate?
maya.finance: Estimate: reserved rate would have reduced billed amount by $9,600 vs burst billed $13,200. Customer paid $13,200; retro allocation would require crediting $3,600. If we issue an operational goodwill credit, recommend rounding to $4,000 for quick resolution and to cover audit convenience.
elena.sales: Customer prefers a corrected invoice for their internal accounting, but they said they'd accept a credit if we provide a formal ledger note.
tom.ops: Root cause: billing snapshot job runs at 07:55 UTC. Provisioning completed ~17 minutes later due to AZ throttling after the TZ cutover. We'll add a guard to delay snapshot when pending provisioning jobs exist.
maya.finance: Need zara.revenue formal approval to apply credit OR legal sign-off to reissue invoice. Also need ops to run this query and paste the exact rows for April 2026:
```
SELECT invoice_id, customer_id, event_time, reserved_tag_state, billing_snapshot_time
FROM provisioning.audit
WHERE customer_id='cust_cardionova' AND date_trunc('month', event_time)='2026-04-01';
```
tom.ops: Query output (pasted): invoice_id=INV-5092, customer_id=cust_cardionova, event_time=2026-04-01T08:12:03Z, reserved_tag_state=active, billing_snapshot_time=2026-04-01T07:55:00Z
zara.revenue: Approve operational credit up to $4,000 conditional on ops adding snapshot guard and a short post-incident note. If customer insists on corrected invoice for auditors, escalate to legal/contracts but we prefer the credit.
maya.finance: Please reply with explicit "approve" to authorize finance to book adjustment. Also ops to confirm ETA for snapshot guard.
elena.sales: I'll loop in CS and the customer with the drafted message: "We identified a timing mismatch during our scheduled timezone migration that caused your reserved commit to miss the billing snapshot. As a remedy we will apply a one-time operational credit of $4,000 and provide a ledger note for your auditors; if you require a corrected invoice we can escalate to legal."
tom.ops: Snapshot guard will be in place by 2026-04-07 17:00 UTC. I'll add runbook entry and link in the follow-up.
zara.revenue: approve
maya.finance: Noted. Creating ledger adjustment ADJ-2026-211 | amount: -4000 | reason: operational_timing_credit | linked_invoice: INV-5092. Finance will attach runbook link and ops note.
billing-bot: Ledger entry created: ADJ-2026-211 | customer: cust_cardionova | amount: -4000 | reason: operational_timing_credit | linked_invoice: INV-5092
elena.sales: Customer notified, CS confirmed acceptance of credit.
tom.ops: Done: snapshot_guard PR merged, runbook created: https://runbooks.redwood/snapshot-guard-2026. Will post postmortem next week.
maya.finance: Closing loop. Finance posted adjustment and added audit note. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
